# API and Data Checklist: Browse the Book Catalogue

**Purpose**: Validate the quality of the API contract and data requirements before implementation begins
**Created**: 2026-09-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the page size stated in the requirements themselves rather than appearing for the first time in the plan? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Is a book's public address, the slug, defined anywhere in the specification, or does it first appear in the data model? [Gap, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the shape of an error response specified in the requirements, beyond saying the wording is clear? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for the order in which authors are presented when a book credits more than one? [Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the expected size of the catalogue stated, so that paging and the loading target can be judged against a number? [Gap, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements defined for where cover art comes from and what constrains it, such as dimensions or hosting? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK007 Are rate limiting or abuse requirements specified for endpoints deliberately reachable without an account? [Gap, Spec §FR-016]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 Is "published" defined in the requirements, given that every read path depends on the distinction? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the search matching rule stated precisely enough to distinguish substring, prefix and whole-word matching? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK010 Is it specified whether a search term of several words must match all of them or any of them? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "a typical mobile connection" quantified with a bandwidth or latency figure? [Clarity, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the statement that listening requires an account specified concretely enough to review, given that no account system exists yet? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK013 Is it stated whether the announced result count covers all matches or only the books on the current page? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK014 Does "every catalogue page" in the indexing requirement include search result pages, which an assumption separately excludes from indexing? [Conflict, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK015 Are cover art requirements consistent between the list and the book page, given that the assumption calls cover art decorative only in the list? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK016 Do the ordering requirement and the search requirement agree on which rules govern matching, as opposed to sorting? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK017 Can the requirement to declare the language of a differing passage be satisfied by a data model that records no language on a book or a chapter? [Conflict, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK018 Does the requirement that no audio location is disclosed hold consistently across both the list and the detail responses? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK019 Can the indexing outcome be objectively verified, given that the timing is controlled by a third party rather than by this system? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the time for a visitor to reach a known book measurable as written, given that it depends on the visitor rather than the system? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the claim that no audio is reachable expressed so that it can be checked exhaustively rather than by sampling? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK022 Does every paging and search requirement have an acceptance scenario that would fail if the requirement were unimplemented? [Traceability, Spec §FR-004]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 Is the response to a page number beyond the last page defined as a requirement, rather than only raised as an open edge case? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements defined for a search term that is empty or contains only whitespace? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK025 Is an upper bound specified for the length of a search term? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements defined for what happens to paging when a book is unpublished between two page requests? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK027 Is a tiebreaker specified for two books whose titles sort identically, given that stable paging depends on a total order? [Gap, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the total running time of a book with no chapters specified, rather than left to the reader to infer? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for chapter positions that are missing, duplicated or not contiguous? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK030 Is the assumption that content arrives only by seeding recorded together with the conditions under which it stops holding? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK031 Is an acceptable delay bounded anywhere between a book being published and its page carrying that book? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the exclusion of accounts, audio and administration stated clearly enough that a reviewer can tell deliberate deferral from oversight? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Several items point at decisions that exist in `plan.md` or `research.md` but not in `spec.md`. Whether that is acceptable is a reviewer judgement: the plan is allowed to decide implementation, but a rule a test must assert belongs in the specification
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
